about: Grammar and logic checks for the Problems panel. 'rules' holds the message, severity and explanation for each check; the logic for each rule id is in the UI's src/ui/js/checks.js. 'controls' lists the per-control files in data/controls/ (in the order the machine picker shows them); each file's 'dialect' holds the per-control data the checks read: modal groups, canned cycle word lists, the words other codes need (wordHints, shown as hint text after the code), codes that mean something else on that control, and limits. 'cycleHelp' (here for the Fanuc-style base, in each control's file for that control) holds the text, sketch and word descriptions for the canned-cycle help dialog. A dialect can inherit from another and override any key; a machine definition file can override severities or turn rules off. Entries marked verified:false were written from general knowledge and still need checking against that control's programming manual.

dup-address.title: Word repeated in a line
dup-address.message: {letter} appears {count} on this line ({words}). The control uses one of them or alarms.
dup-address.why: Each address letter except G and M can appear once per block.

unbalanced-brackets.title: Brackets that don't match
unbalanced-brackets.message: {word} has {open} [ and {close} ]. The control alarms when it reads this line.
unbalanced-brackets.why: Every [ in an expression needs a ] to close it.

modal-group-clash.title: Two codes from one group
modal-group-clash.message: {codes} are both {group} codes. Only one can be active, so the control alarms or uses the last one.
modal-group-clash.why: Codes in the same modal group cancel each other.

m-conflict.title: M-codes that contradict each other
m-conflict.message: {codes} on the same line contradict each other.

cycle-needs-feed-per-min.title: Cycle needs a feed per minute
cycle-needs-feed-per-min.message: {cycle} ({name}) runs in {perRev} (feed per rev) here, but no {perMin} feed was programmed before it. The control alarms.
cycle-needs-feed-per-min.why: With the main spindle stopped, the cycle can't feed per rev; it uses the last feed per minute.

cycle-call-no-def.title: Cycle call with no cycle
cycle-call-no-def.message: {word} runs a cycle, but no CYCL DEF comes before it.

pgm-name-mismatch.title: Program names don't match
pgm-name-mismatch.message: END PGM {end} doesn't match BEGIN PGM {begin}.

block-number-order.title: Block numbers out of order
block-number-order.why: The control numbers blocks in order from 0. Out-of-order numbers usually mean lines were pasted in from another program.

pattern-no-cycle.title: Pattern with nothing to repeat
pattern-no-cycle.message: {code} ({name}) machines the active canned cycle at each point, but no canned cycle or (MCALL) is active here.
pattern-no-cycle.why: A multiple-machining pattern repeats the canned cycle or modal subroutine that's active. Without one, the tool only moves.

cycle-stray-word.title: Word the cycle doesn't use
cycle-stray-word.message: {cycle} ({name}) doesn't use {word}, so it is ignored or alarms.

missing-label.title: Jump to a label that isn't there
missing-label.message: {word} points to {label}, which isn't in this file.

no-feed-rate.title: Feed move with no feed rate
no-feed-rate.message: This {move} runs at feed rate, but no F has been set yet.
no-feed-rate.why: Most controls alarm on the first feed move without F; some reuse a stale value.

feed-mode-changed.title: Feed rate from the other feed mode
feed-mode-changed.message: F{f} was set under {old} but {new} is active now, so it reads as {reading}.
feed-mode-changed.why: F is not cleared when G94/G95 changes.

feed-plausibility.title: Feed rate looks like the wrong mode
feed-plausibility.message: F{f} {unit} is unusually {size}. Check that {mode} is the mode you meant.

spindle-off-feed.title: Cutting with the spindle stopped
spindle-off-feed.message: This {move} cuts while the spindle is stopped ({spin}).

torch-off-cut.title: Feed move with the torch off
torch-off-cut.message: This {move} runs at feed rate while the torch is off ({state}).
torch-off-cut.why: A plasma program turns the torch on before each cut and off after it, and travels between cuts with G00. A feed move with the torch off usually means the cut on code is missing.

torch-on-at-end.title: Torch on at program end
torch-on-at-end.message: The program ends with the torch on ({code} is active). Turn it off with {off} first.

no-speed.title: Spindle started with no speed
no-speed.message: {code} starts the spindle but no S has been set.

arc-no-center.title: Arc with no center or radius
arc-no-center.message: {code} needs {radius} or {centers} to define the arc.

arc-r-and-ijk.title: Arc with both R and center
arc-r-and-ijk.message: This arc has both {radius} and {centers}. Most controls use {radius} and ignore the others.

arc-full-circle-r.title: Full circle written with R
arc-full-circle-r.message: The arc starts and ends at the same point, which {radius} can't describe. Use {centers}.

arc-radius-mismatch.title: Arc end isn't on the circle
arc-radius-mismatch.message: Start is {r1} from the center but the end is {r2} from it (off by {diff}).

comp-start-on-arc.title: Cutter comp started on an arc
comp-start-on-arc.message: {code} has to start on a G00 or G01 move, not an arc.

comp-no-d.title: Cutter comp with no D offset
comp-no-d.message: {code} turns on cutter comp but no D offset has been given.

tlo-missing.title: Z move with no tool length offset
tlo-missing.message: First Z move after the tool change on {line}, but {tlo} hasn't been called for this tool.

tlo-h-mismatch.title: Length offset doesn't match tool
tlo-h-mismatch.message: {h} is used with {t}. Usually the H number matches the tool number.

cycle-left-on.title: Canned cycle still active
cycle-left-on.message: {cycle} is still active at the {event}. Add G80 first.

comp-left-on.title: Cutter comp still active
comp-left-on.message: {comp} is still active at the {event}. Add G40 first.

g28-absolute.title: G28 in absolute mode
g28-absolute.message: G28 under G90 moves through work position {axes} on the way home. Use G28 G91 with {zeros} instead.

css-no-clamp.title: Surface speed with no RPM limit
css-no-clamp.message: G96 is on but no {clamp} max RPM has been set. Small diameters can overspeed the spindle.

dwell-no-time.title: Dwell with no time
dwell-no-time.message: G04 needs {words} for the dwell time.

dwell-milliseconds.title: Dwell in milliseconds
dwell-milliseconds.message: {word} has no decimal point, so this control reads it as {ms} milliseconds ({sec} s). Write {word}. if you mean {ms} seconds.

m-per-block.title: Too many M-codes in a line
m-per-block.message: This control allows {max} M-code per line, and this line has {count} ({words}).

rapid-below-zero.title: Rapid below Z0
rapid-below-zero.message: Rapid to Z{z}, below Z0. If Z0 is the top of the part, this rapids into it.

missing-decimal.title: Number with no decimal point
missing-decimal.message: {word} has no decimal point, so the control reads it as {letter}{value} {unit}. Write {letter}{intended} if you mean {amount} {unit}.
missing-decimal.why: Fanuc-style controls read a whole number on a distance word as the smallest increment (0.0001 in or 0.001 mm).

unknown-word.title: Word not in the dictionary
unknown-word.message: {word} isn't in the dictionary or this machine's file.

router.label: Router
router.about: A router reads G code the way its control's mill does; a control lists router (even empty) when it's made for routers.

plasma.label: Plasma
plasma.about: A plasma machine starts from its control's mill tables and words, then the control's plasma table on top (fanuc.plasma for the Fanuc-style chain). A control with no mill tables (Hypertherm) has only its plasma table. timeline lists the values the Z-by-line timeline can plot, the first being the default: z (or x, the lathe radius), feed (the feed rate) and speed (the spindle speed while it turns). A machine with a process (process.on) also shows a band where the torch is on and marks the lines with a process.changes code (a material or process change, since plasma power is set on the power supply, not in the program).

fileHints.about: Clues that suggest which control a file was written for when it's opened and has no default yet. A matching clue puts its controls in a Suggested group at the top of the machine picker and picks the first one; nothing is chosen without the user. Content clues are regular expressions tried on the first 64 KB and count more than the extension. Only list clues that belong to one control family: .nc and .tap are used by too many controls to suggest anything.

content.why: RTS at the end of a subprogram
Haas codes (G187, G154 P or M97)

cycleHelp.about: Text for the canned-cycle help dialog. Each word entry is [example value, what it does] or [example value, what it does, gloss word]; the gloss word replaces the usual one while that cycle is active (Haas G76 A60 reads ANGLE60, not ?A60). 'common' words apply to every cycle of that machine type. Keys like 'haas.lathe', in that control's file (data/controls/haas.json), override the Fanuc-style base for that control. 'sketch' picks the drawing; 'labels' renames the letters on it. A cycle with 'needs' in the dialect table (such as liveTooling) is offered only on machine profiles that have that option.

X: Hole position in X. After this line, every line with just X or Y drills another hole, until G80.
R: Retract plane. The tool rapids down to R, then feeds from there. G99 comes back up to R between holes, G98 to where it started.
K: How many times to run the hole. Under G91, each repeat steps over by X and Y.
L: How many times to run the hole. L0 sets up the cycle without drilling here.
P: Dwell at the bottom, in seconds on Haas (P0.5). Fanuc takes milliseconds with no decimal point (P500).

G73.about: Drills to Z in pecks of Q. After each peck the tool backs off a little to break the chip, without leaving the hole. Faster than G83, but it doesn't clear chips out of deep holes.

G74.about: Left-hand tapping. The spindle runs in reverse down to Z, then reverses at the bottom and feeds back out to R.

F: Feed. Must equal the thread pitch times the RPM (1/16 pitch at 500 rpm is 31.25 in/min), or the pitch itself under G95.

G76.about: Bores to Z, stops the spindle in a set orientation, moves the tool away from the wall by Q, then rapids out so the tip doesn't drag a line up the bore.

Q: How far the tool moves off the wall before it pulls out.

G81.about: The plain drilling cycle: rapid to R, feed to Z, rapid back out.

G82.about: Like G81, but it pauses at the bottom for P so a spot drill or counterbore leaves a clean, flat bottom.

G83.about: Drills in pecks of Q and rapids all the way back up to R after each peck to clear the chips. Use it for deep holes.

G84.about: Right-hand tapping. Feeds to Z, reverses the spindle at the bottom and feeds back out to R.

F: Feed. Must equal the thread pitch times the RPM (1/16 pitch at 500 rpm is 31.25 in/min), or the pitch itself under G95.

G85.about: Feeds to Z and feeds back out to R. For reaming and boring, where a rapid out would mark the wall.

G86.about: Feeds to Z, stops the spindle and rapids out. The tip drags up the wall, so it's for rough boring.

G87.about: Back boring. The tool goes down through the hole shifted off center, moves back to center by Q, starts the spindle and cuts upward to Z.

Z: Top of the back bore (where the upward cut stops).
R: Start of the cut, below the part.
Q: How far the tool is shifted to pass through the hole.

G89.about: Like G85 with a dwell: feeds to Z, pauses for P, feeds back out.

U: Incremental X distance (on the diameter), used instead of X.
W: Incremental Z distance, used instead of Z.

G70.about: Runs the finished contour once, from the line numbered P to the line numbered Q, taking off the stock the roughing cycle left.

P: N number of the first line of the contour.
Q: N number of the last line of the contour.
F: Finish feed, if the contour lines don't give one.

G71.about: Roughs away the stock down to the contour between lines P and Q, in passes along Z, and leaves U and W for G70 to finish. On Fanuc it takes two lines: the first (G71 U R) sets the depth of cut and retract, the second names the contour.

U: Finish stock left on X for G70, as a diameter.
W: Finish stock left on Z for G70.
P: N number of the first line of the contour.
Q: N number of the last line of the contour.

G72.about: Like G71, but the passes run along X, facing down from the end of the part. Good for parts wider than they are long.

U: Finish stock left on X for G70, as a diameter.
W: Finish stock left on Z for G70.
P: N number of the first line of the contour.
Q: N number of the last line of the contour.

G76.about: Cuts a whole thread in many passes. Each pass feeds in along the flank and takes a little less than the last, so the chip load stays even. On Fanuc it takes two lines: the first (G76 P Q R) sets finishing passes, chamfer, tool angle and the smallest cut; the second, shown here, gives the size.

X: Minor diameter at the end of the thread (the last pass).
P: Thread height (radius) in 0.0001 in with no decimal point. P383 is 0.0383.
Q: Depth of the first pass, same units. Q120 is 0.012.
F: Lead: the distance between threads. 16 per inch is 0.0625.
R: Taper: X difference from the end to the start, as a radius. 0 for a straight thread.

G90.about: One turning pass as a box: rapid to X, feed to Z, feed back out, rapid back to the start. Repeat the line with smaller X values for more passes.

Z: Where the pass ends in Z.
R: Taper: X difference from start to end, as a radius.

G92.about: One threading pass as a box: rapid to X, thread to Z at the lead F, rapid out and back. Write one line per pass, each a little deeper.

R: Taper: X difference from start to end, as a radius.

G94.about: One facing pass as a box: rapid to Z, feed down to X, feed back out, rapid back. Repeat with smaller Z values for more passes.

X: Diameter where the face pass stops.
R: Cone: Z difference across the face.
